name: Gabriel Skantze
focus: Conversational systems, feedback and turn-taking at KTH.
exercise: Read the Voice Activity Projection paper. Draw two speakers’ activity on one clock and mark where a silence-only baseline cannot distinguish two different future turns.

name: Hema A. Murthy
focus: Signal processing and synthesis for Indian languages at IIT Madras.
exercise: Read the Prakash–Murthy study on language-family transfer. Design a comparison that fixes target-speaker data minutes and holds out names and phonemic contrasts.

name: Shinji Watanabe
focus: End-to-end speech processing and reproducible speech recipes at Carnegie Mellon.
exercise: Pair the ESPnet paper with one repository recipe. Write down the split, tokenizer and scoring command before comparing a result.

name: Simon King
focus: Synthetic speech perception and listening-study design at Edinburgh.
exercise: Read the dual-task listening study with Avashna Govender. Predict the natural-speech baseline, then inspect why the authors question a single interpretation.

name: KTH Speech, Music and Hearing
focus: Speech communication, perception and multimodal interaction.
exercise: Find a turn-taking project, identify what each time-aligned channel observes and specify the perceptual cue a transcript-only baseline loses.

name: Centre for Speech Technology Research
focus: Speech research and Blizzard Challenge listening resources at Edinburgh.
exercise: Compare the test material and conditions of use for two Blizzard Challenge editions. Design a counterbalanced listening trial with an original passage.

name: Kyutai
focus: Open research on real-time speech models including Moshi.
exercise: Read the Moshi technical report alongside its implementation. Trace one codec frame through the separate conversational streams and list the clocks a latency study needs.

name: Praat
focus: Open-source speech measurement, annotation and synthesis tools.
exercise: Measure the same synthetic tone at two analysis window lengths. Include the settings with a small script and describe what a wider window resolves.

name: ESPnet
focus: End-to-end speech processing with versioned recipes and scoring steps.
exercise: Choose a small example and inspect its data preparation, tokenizer and scoring stages. Prepare a normalization regression case that uses synthetic text.

name: pyannote.audio
focus: Open-source building blocks for speaker diarization.
exercise: Write a two-speaker overlap annotation and compare time scored with and without overlap. Check a pipeline’s model terms and access requirements before downloading it.

name: SpeechBrain
focus: Open-source speech recipes and components for conversational AI.
exercise: Read the contribution guidelines and prepare a local, minimal example that exercises an edge case in a recipe or documentation snippet.
